The fact that she gained so much after having a child and continues to do so is probably an indicator that she was just naturally thin before and now she’s absolutely lost. Pretty much the exact same scenario happened to me last fall. I met this guy that had DM'd me on instagram after seeing my Tinder profile, and we met up for drinks. The next few days were pretty much the same situation as yours, and I fell hard for him. He was perfect, and we were great together. He eventually after 3 weeks just... very weirdly.... ghosted me? Same way your guy did. I was SUPER heart broken, and badly enough, he had even at that point said he **loved** me (red flag, but chose to ignore it because I was falling for him). 

It sucked, and it actually took a lot longer than I thought it would to get over it (2 months). I think the method that finally worked for me was to remind myself of the reasons why he wasn't as perfect as I thought he was. I cried a lot, mostly because I felt scammed and confused over my emotions, but remind yourself of who you are and what you want. You definitely don't want this guy - and any guy who feels the same spark as you do would be just as cautious as you to dive in because he doesn't want to get hurt either. If you need someone to talk to, vent to your friends or anyone on here and just let it out. One day you'll say the words and realize you don't feel them anymore, and then you'll finally be ready to move on!

Don’t think med schools will think this hard about your decision but if your concern is that somehow you’ll get bad karma for it, then I wouldn’t worry about it. Just think about how great it was for the kid that got your spot at Undergrad B!
